review_process.scope: Three supplemental real public PR captures across two repositories; not customer evidence. Original 36-case benchmark excluded.
limitations: AI review only; no independent human adjudication.
Reviewers may share a model family and correlated errors remain possible.
Manifest selection metadata was visible, but is not used as expected-outcome evidence.

adjudication.rationale: Original independently authored labels frozen before cross-review. An empty conflict list does not mean adjudication has occurred.

documentation.use: Original pre-output readiness, assurance, identity, policy, checks and review method; unchanged.
Outcome vocabularies and label structure; arithmetic contract unchanged.
REST PR mergeability is a bounded GitHub observation; the page did not establish that the divergent captured PR-base SHA and current branch-tip SHA may be silently treated as one coherent identity.
Branch protected/unprotected metadata is an independent policy observation. The branch-list documentation distinguishes protection by branch protections or rulesets.

observed_github_operational_status.summary: Open, non-draft, mergeable=true and mergeable_state=clean in both PR observations; effective review decision APPROVED. These are GitHub operational observations, not fully observed supported assurance.

mandatory_requirements.rationale: Branch policy lists the context with app_id null, GraphQL marks it is_required=true for this PR, and REST shows success on the same observed head. Full target-base coherence remains a separate unresolved prerequisite.

No observed merge conflict at the captured PR identity.
required_observations.rationale: Both observations say mergeable=true. This is not a complete policy or release assurance statement.

required_observations.requirement: The PR/base and observed target branch must support a coherent identity before a positive bounded assurance claim.
required_observations.rationale: Both initial/final PR base snapshots disagree with both target-branch tip snapshots. Repetition establishes stability within each endpoint, not coherence between them. No captured relationship or refresh result resolves the difference.

required_observations.requirement: Discover the applicable mandatory branch/review policy sufficiently to support ready/pass.
required_observations.rationale: The branch is protected, but detailed status/review policy reads are denied. Named required checks and APPROVED are observable; full strict-up-to-date and required-review policy details are not. The active copilot_code_review rule describes automated review behavior and does not by itself establish an approval merge gate or a failure.

policy_observations.denied_endpoint_interpretation: HTTP 403 Resource not accessible by integration is denied access, never an empty policy response. Absence of an Authorization header supplied by capture code does not establish an anonymous upstream transport.

empty_combined_status.rationale: pending with total_count=0 and no statuses does not establish a failed or pending mandatory context. Statuses and check runs are separate surfaces.

unknowns.description: The PR base SHA and current same-named branch SHA differ throughout the capture. The raw snapshot does not prove that the mergeability result, applicable policy, and observed evidence share one target-base identity.
unknowns.effect: Prevents ready/pass; does not itself establish a merge blocker or a strict up-to-date policy failure.

unknowns.description: Classic protection is enabled, but full required status checks and required review policy reads return HTTP 403. The branch response exposes three required check names, null app bindings, and non_admins enforcement; it does not expose strict or review-policy parameters. APPROVED and successful checks cannot enumerate denied policy facts.
unknowns.effect: Independent policy-discovery reason for unknown/unknown, without inventing a failed hidden requirement.

unsupported_policy_limitations: Strict/up-to-date status and required-review policy parameters (such as approval count, dismissal, code-owner or last-push requirements) are not observed because detail endpoints are denied. Their applicability or failure is not assumed.

collection_limitations.description: Only PR and branch identity are re-read at the end. Reviews/checks/policy are individual observations within the short interval, not an atomic snapshot. No change to those states is observed, so this limitation does not invent an additional confirmed blocker.
Effective upstream identity and scopes are unobservable; the capture reports no Authorization header supplied by code and possible inherited-proxy authentication.
GraphQL asks for first:100 context nodes without pageInfo. The visible node count equals the complete captured REST check count and is below 100; no observed truncation is asserted.

legacy_compatibility.basis: The observed REST PR summary is open, non-draft, mergeable=true, mergeable_state=clean on both observations. Those factual GitHub summaries permit the historical operational ready vocabulary. This annotation neither predicts producer behavior nor overrides conservative unknown readiness/assurance.

confidence.basis: The cited source facts directly establish the unresolved base-identity difference and absence of any captured applicable failure. Confidence concerns this bounded label, not live PR safety.

cases.rationale: The PR is operationally clean and approved; all three explicitly required build checks succeed at the captured head. There is no confirmed blocker. Conservative readiness and scoped assurance remain unknown because protected-branch detail discovery is denied and the PR base identity differs from the stable target-branch identity. Neither clean mergeability nor successful visible evidence repairs those gaps.
